react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converged on arachidonic acid metabolism as the dominant biological signal in the treatment-versus-control comparison. RaMP-DB ORA (multi-DB hypergeometric) ranked Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) first with an FDR of 6.84e-14, driven by five arachidonic acid–derived oxylipids (5-HETE, 15-HETE, LTA4, 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2, and arachidonic acid itself); this was the single most significant result across all tools. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA returned KEGG:hsa00590 (Arachidonic acid metabolism) with a raw p-value of 1.0 and an observed-to-expected ratio of 4 of 4 possible input hits — a clean, complete overlap of every annotated arachidonate-derived input in this KEGG-subset run. Mummichog m/z-direct activity analysis also ranked Arachidonic acid metabolism first (p = 0.004) and independently recovered Leukotriene metabolism (p = 0.026), Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate (p = 0.044), and Glycerophospholipid metabolism (p = 0.026) in the top six, providing network-empirical corroboration of the ORA result. Glycolaldehyde (KEGG:C00266) appeared in the Mummichog Glycerophospholipid metabolism and Glycolysis/Gluconeogenesis hits, reflecting its role as a two-carbon oxidation product that can be incorporated into lipid biosynthetic networks. Losartan (KEGG:C07072) did not map to any human endogenous pathway in this analysis, consistent with its identity as an exogenously administered angiotensin-II receptor antagonist rather than a de novo biosynthetic metabolite. The cross-paradigm consensus identifies arachidonic acid as the upstream precursor and the five oxylipid derivatives as the primary signal mediators, implicating coordinated activation of COX/PTGS and 5-LOX/ALOX pathways in the treatment condition.

The m/z-direct Mummichog network also ranked MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism first (p=0.000672) and recovered eight of its 11 pathway members from the input set, including all five eicosanoid markers plus three additional HETE intermediates.
